method: Official public website and documentation review; authenticated application was not inspected. Approved V6 images control appearance.

sources.observed: A dedicated product page explains the central capability, demonstrates the workflow, groups practical uses and ends with conversion and a full footer.
sources.adaptation: Avenor Product page explains reserve, verify and decide using release planning rather than autonomous coding.

sources.observed: Security has a dedicated destination covering data handling, auditability and access enforcement, with a path to further assessment.
sources.adaptation: Avenor Security focuses on scoped roles, review gates and an audit-event example. No real certification claims or badges are borrowed.

sources.observed: Enterprise documentation makes deployment boundaries and responsibility choices explicit before technical configuration.
sources.adaptation: Show how Avenor keeps environment access separate from approval authority and presents a practical security review request.

sources.observed: The documented first session is context gathering followed by review of a bounded proposed change. It then expands to connected systems and repeatable workflows.
sources.adaptation: The app sequence opens the release schedule, reviews six verification results, then inspects owners. The component requests a change without falsely approving or starting a rollout.

originality: All product copy, sample people, service data and composition are original fictional Avenor content; source sites provide UX purposes, not designs to duplicate.

captures.observedVisualUX: The page uses a dedicated security title, concise opening CTA, grouped trust topics, related content and a full multi-column footer; mobile stacks the subjects and condenses navigation. Avenor replaces the source branding, certification marks, dark sections and AI claims with a light permissions and audit narrative.
